text:
support-esc: FYI customer ACME just escalated — p95 for /v1/generate jumped ~2x starting ~03:10 UTC. They sent traces and said UX is degraded. Ticket #INC-12345. Screenshot attached. @lex @kari :exclamation:
lex: pulling metrics. which dashboard are they looking at? link? :eyes:
support-esc: They pointed to the ‘API latency / p95 (global)’ panel in prod -> model-serving -> last 6h. It shows a stair-step at 03:10. p99 also spikes but report says p95 impact is biggest for them.
kari: I see the same on the panel. But raw histogram panel (per-request buckets) doesn't show as big a shift — more of a right tail growth. Could be a rollup vs raw-aggregation mismatch.
devon: can we get a raw event sample? run the ClickHouse/metrics query for the raw request durations (not rollup). I suspect host-level skew or sampling change.
lex: running raw query now (clickhouse):
```
SELECT toStartOfFiveMinute(ts) as window, quantileExact(0.95)(duration_ms) as p95, count()
FROM http_requests
WHERE route = '/v1/generate' AND env='prod' AND ts >= now() - INTERVAL 6 HOUR
GROUP BY window
ORDER BY window
```
lex: raw quantileExact shows a small bump at 03:10, but not 2x. Rollup panel shows 2x.
pj: last deploy at 02:58 was a model config change + routing tweak that enabled fallback-candidates. deploy-bot: canary promoted at 03:05.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary promoted to 40% at 03:05, promoted to 100% at 03:09 (auto).
kari: ah — auto-promoted at 03:09. that aligns. Maybe canary exposes short-lived tail in some hosts that rollup interprets differently.
support-esc: customer timeline matches that promotion window.
devon: Differences often come from two things: 1) the dashboard panel uses rollup-averaged p95 (e.g., compute p95 per host then avg), 2) the histogram buckets used by one panel are aggregated differently (bucket boundaries or downsample). Can anyone check how the dashboard panel is defined?
lex: panel config excerpt:
```yaml
panel: api_latency_p95_global
source: metrics.rollups
aggregation: avg_over_hosts(quantile(0.95))
window: 5m
```
lex: it's doing avg_over_hosts of per-host quantiles. That can amplify changes if one host jumps to higher p95.
kari: good catch. raw events show one AZ/instance having repeated auth retries that cause ~800ms extra per request. If per-host p95 spikes there, averaging hosts will affect global.
devon: can we find traces from that host? filter trace id from logs. run:
```bash
curl -s "https://logs.internal/api/search?service=model-serving&from=03:00&to=03:20&query=trace_id:*") | jq '.hits[] | select(.host=="i-az3-17")]'
```
lex: found traces: trace=tr_0a1b2c3d showing repeated 401->retry attempts, header shows retry=3 + backoff. payload small but latency adds up. snippet:
```
[03:11:02Z] trace=tr_0a1b2c3d host=i-az3-17 route=/v1/generate status=200 duration_ms=1120 note="auth-retry=2"
[03:11:03Z] trace=tr_0a1b2c3e host=i-az3-17 route=/v1/generate status=200 duration_ms=980 note="auth-retry=1"
```
pj: that host had a token fetch error against KMS region timeout earlier, fixed by redispatch at 03:12 but the tail persisted for a few minutes. Looks like the fallback candidate code path retries auth sync and adds latency.
kari: so root cause likely the canary changed fallback behavior plus an intermittent KMS latency, concentrating retries on one host. Dashboard rollup (avg of per-host p95) exaggerated global p95.
support-esc: customer wants mitigation now. Options?
devon: quick mitigations: 1) rollback canary to previous routing (fast but churn), 2) temporary route traffic away from the problematic host (drain i-az3-17), 3) change dashboard to show global quantile (quantileExact over all events) to avoid confusion for ops/internal visibility. For customer-facing SLA, we should: drain host and roll back auto-promotion.
lex: I can run a host-drain and revert auto-promotion flag. Steps:
1) kubectl annotate deployment model-serving action=drain-host i-az3-17
2) set featureflag(fallback-sync-retries)=false in config-store (runtime)
3) trigger rollback of canary via deploy service: POST /deploys/rollback?canary=1723456
I'll do 1 and 2 now.
ops-bot: action: host-drain queued on i-az3-17.
lex: host drain in progress. requests redirected. monitoring: creating a temporary global-quantile panel and updating incident channel.
(1 minute later)
lex: after drain, p95 panel (global-quantile) shows regression resolved back to baseline; rollup avg still elevated for a single 5m window due to earlier data points.
kari: to avoid recurring confusion: update dashboard docstring and change that panel to quantileExact over raw events. Also add host-level heatmap and an annotation showing deploy events.
devon: follow-ups: - add a test that ensures auto-promote respects fallback retry budget, - add metric for KMS latency so we can detect cross-service fragility early, - review rollout policy to require 15m canary with slower promotion unless no retries in logs.
support-esc: relaying mitigation to ACME (we drained host + rolled back auto-promote). they asked for a postmortem.
pj: I'll own the postmortem. initial notes: timeline, root cause = fallback retries + KMS timeout + rollup panel amplification, mitigations taken, long-term actions.
ops-bot: incident created INC-12345, severity: S2, assignee: pj.
support-esc: customer confirmed degraded UX improved after 03:16. closing loop and will request a follow-up call if they see anything else.
lex: adding dashboards patch and issuing PR to change panel aggregation. will tag @kari @pj for review.
pj: thanks everyone. please add any logs/traces to the incident doc. :thumbsup:
